## Why visit

An attractive Pennine village brewpub where the beer’s place of production is part of the experience. The brewery is visible from the bar, and Ossett’s 2026 account confirms continued onsite brewing after its move to the ground floor. The riverside setting gives a different outing from the two big cities, particularly with a daylight village or canal walk. It is a sensible alternative for lovers of local cask and landscape, but requires transport checks and should replace another excursion rather than overload five days. Busy Saturday ale-trail traffic can make a quieter visit more rewarding.

## Beer

Riverhead ales brewed onsite, Ossett beers and guests; CAMRA reports a broad cask selection with dark beer usually represented.

## Cider and perry

**Real cider documented; reconfirm stock.** CAMRA records occasional real cider, so availability is intermittent rather than a reason to travel solely for cider.

See [how cider is classified](../real-cider.md).

## Food

Official site advertises bao and loaded fries/Asian street food; CAMRA notes no meals Monday/Tuesday. Confirm kitchen days.

## Plan the visit

Check rail engineering and the last return. Saturdays can be busy; onsite brewing does not promise a scheduled tour.

**Getting there:** Marsden station when services operate; allow a village walk to the pub and verify replacement transport.

Check [November transport issues](../logistics.md) for date-specific disruption.
